display.purpose: The wordmark (in the app bar and on the sign-in screen), the reader title, the page headings such as Settings and Import, and the empty-library heading. 24px in List, 30px in Grid, 0.85 under 760px, except that the reader title and the page headings never go under --rd-title-min (1.1) times Headline, 22px at the default 16px browser font. The two wordmarks and the empty-library heading keep the 0.85 scale. These three have no minimum against Headline, because they are not reading headings, so at a very small browser font they can fall under it; only the 12px text floor (--t-floor-ui) holds them.

headline.purpose: Reader section headings such as Original post, Comments and README, and the heading of each sign-in and setup screen. Never under the 16px reading floor divided by --post-h-cap (about 16.84px).

title.purpose: Item titles in rows and cards. An unread title takes --dw-strong, 700 in the default Library pair; Instrument Serif and the Cal.com Style have one display weight, so there the Read state mark alone marks it, in the Item list, in Grid and on a Topic page.

body.purpose: Post, comment and summary text in the reading column, at the Text width measure.

body-list.purpose: Interface text of fields, dialogs, page sections and the Highlights and Proposals lists; size follows Density.

meta.purpose: The default UI size: metadata, buttons, filters and bylines.

label.purpose: Uppercase names of controls, filter groups, settings groups and data fields.

strip.purpose: The kept strip, and the counts and times around it: the wordmark's count, chip, segment and row counts, Index counts, row metadata, Highlights and Log times, Proposal counts.

code.purpose: Code blocks; inline code keeps the surrounding size.

shadows.name: shadow
shadows.purpose: Low: the sheet's side buttons, the focused skip button and the Grid cards of the Styles other than Library (Light theme).

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: High: the settings panel, the reader sheet and the floating paste card (Light theme).

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Reading Room"**

Threadsift is a quiet library room. The saved text leads, and the interface stays in the background. The mood is quiet, bookish and exact. Chrome is drawn in near-white surfaces, cool greys and hairlines, and one accent hue marks state. The reading column holds post and comment text at one size and one line length. The metadata, controls and lists around it are smaller and greyer than that text.

This file describes the app as built. Its last section, Brand Brief, describes the target look, the Quarto direction. Where the two differ, a change to the app follows the earlier sections, and the Quarto kit in the prototype and the build of Quarto follow the Brand Brief.

The look is not one preset. Every Look setting is a `data-*` attribute on the app root, and each option swaps a set of tokens; Theme and Layout are attributes on the same root. `design/system/tokens.css` is the source every value is read from, except the literal values its header lists, and `design/system/settings-table.ts` owns the list of settings and which option is the default. The tokens in this file record the default look: the Library Style, Light theme, the Library font pair (Schibsted Grotesk and Commit Mono), Moss accent, Medium text size, Medium text width, Compact density and the List layout.

Density is compact by default, because a library with hundreds of saves needs many rows on screen, but the reading column never gets denser with it. Components are refined and restrained. Two looks are rejected. One is a social feed: Reddit's or X's own chrome, with vote arrows, avatars ahead of the item title, and engagement counts as the loudest thing on a row. The other is a SaaS dashboard: gradient hero cards, number tiles and icons in coloured circles.
keyCharacteristics: One accent hue on neutrals with almost no colour, the same in List and Grid; Sepia is the one warm Theme. The theme sets the accent's lightness and chroma.
One reading size and one capped line length for post, comment and summary text.
Flat hairline structure in List and Grid: a Grid card is a cell of one ruled table. Soft shadows sit only on floating layers.
Every value is a token, except the literal values the `design/system/tokens.css` header lists, and every Look option is a token swap on the app root.
The app answers to its own width, through `data-bp`, in five bands.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent is the one colour that marks selection, action and state. The tag hues, the paste card's status tones, the `warn` colour of field errors, delete buttons and the failure mark on an Item row, and the accent swatches in the settings panel are the only other colours in the chrome. A full accent fill covers nothing larger than a control, a dot or a bar. A larger selected area, such as the open row, takes the soft tint.

rules.name: The Theme Owns Lightness Rule
rules.body: An accent sets hue only. Each theme sets the accent's lightness and chroma (`--acc-l`, `--acc-c`, `--acc-ink`), so every accent meets the contrast floor in every theme without its own per-theme values.

rules.name: The One Reading Size Rule
rules.body: Post, comment and summary text share one size (`--t-read`). Headings inside a post render at that same size, but never over `--post-h-cap` (0.95) times Headline, so the reader's section headings (`--t-h2`) always outrank them, at a Large Text size too, and the page reads in outline order.

rules.name: The Plain Panel Rule
rules.body: The settings panel keeps the Library pair whatever the Font setting is, so the controls that change the font never move.

rules.name: The Open Word Rule
rules.body: Display, page and section headings and item titles take the Font's display letter and word spacing (`--dls`, `--dws`). The Library pair tightens the letters by 0.015em and opens each word space by 0.05em, so a tight grotesque title still reads as separate words.

rules.name: The Still Root Rule
rules.body: The app root never scrolls. Each pane scrolls itself, and keeping an item in view scrolls only its own pane.

rules.name: The Own Width Rule
rules.body: Layout responds to the app's width through `data-bp`, never to the window through a media query.

rules.name: The Lifted Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the element sits above the page: a floating layer. Rows, Library Grid cards, panes and boxes inside the reader stay flat.

dos: **Do** take every value from a token in `design/system/tokens.css`. The only literals are the ones the header of that file lists.
**Do** add a new Look option as a `data-*` rule on the app root that lists only the tokens it changes, and add the option to the settings table in `design/system/settings-table.ts`.
**Do** keep every text and background pair at 4.5:1 or more, and every mark, icon and border a person needs to see a control or its state at 3:1 or more, in every theme with every accent and Style.

**Do** draw the edge in the control line colour (`--ctl-line`) when the edge is what shows the control, such as a field or a read Item's Read state mark. It measures 3:1 or more against the page, the surfaces and the open row's tint, in every theme with every accent. The hairline colours (`--line`, `--line-2`) measure 1.2 to 2.1:1 against the page and both surfaces, so they only separate regions or edge a control that shows visible text. Both figures are WCAG relative-luminance ratios computed from the OKLCH values in `tokens.css`.

**Do** make every target at least 44px under 480px, except the width of a link or a Highlight mark in the text of a rendered post or comment (`.md`), a code block included. Each keeps the width of its text, so two marks side by side never share a tap area, and `--link-pad` sets its height. A mark that wraps a picture has the picture's size (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, [Inline exception](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)).
**Do** mark the open row and the open Grid card with an edge as well as a tint.
**Do** give every animation a reduced-motion form.
**Do** keep the reading column at the Text width setting's measure, and keep the Read state mark at the start of the kept strip, never on a picture.
donts: **Don't** build a social feed's chrome: vote arrows, avatars ahead of an item's title in the list, or engagement counts as the loudest thing on a row.
**Don't** build a SaaS dashboard: gradient hero cards, number tiles, or icons in coloured circles.
**Don't** fill an area larger than a control with the full accent. Use the soft tint.
**Don't** scroll the app root, and don't use media queries for width. Read `data-bp`.
**Don't** give List rows, Library Grid cards, panes or reader boxes an elevation shadow.
